sermon.title: Partake of Jesus
sermon.speaker: Michael Silla
sermon.summary: This message shows how Moses and Israel’s journey picture Jesus: the Passover, the Red Sea as baptism, forty days of fasting and manna from heaven. Jesus is the true bread of life, and we must partake of him—not just hear or carry the word. Through Emmaus and the prodigal son, the speaker urges taking the whole bread, judgment and mercy alike, and letting the word give us life.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Delivered by a speaker other than Pastor Kincer (likely Michael Silla—confirm). Points to check: “happy 4:2” = Matthew 4:2; “1 Corinthians 10 1 verse 5” read as 10:1–5; Moses’ forty days placed right after the Red Sea; “Did Jesus really need to get water baptized probably not he is baptism.” Sensitive content: none notable.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Where your fathers tested Me, tried Me, And saw My works forty years. Therefore I was angry with that generation, And said, ‘They always go astray in their heart, And they have not known My ways.’ So I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall not enter My rest.’ ” Beware, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God; but exhort one another daily, while it is called “Today,” lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. For we have become partakers of Christ if we hold the beginning of our confidence steadfast to the end, while it is said: “Today, if you will hear His voice, Do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.” For who, having heard, rebelled? Indeed, was it not all who came out of Egypt, led by Moses? Now with whom was He angry forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose corpses fell in the wilderness? And to whom did He swear that they would not enter His rest, but to those who did not obey? So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.

chunks.section_question: What does the prodigal son teach?
chunks.short_answer: Luke 15:17–18: he came to his senses—my father’s servants have bread to spare—and went back. If you don’t partake you have no life; be a doer of the word, not only a hearer.
chunks.text:
You’re pressing in to find that piece of value and if you don’t do those things you’re not going to find that wonderful piece of value as a young person when I first experienced Jesus Christ I would experience him every day but that went away over time why because we have to pursue we have to go after the value we have to use the tools that it takes to dig up the ground to get to the coal to break open the coal oh that’s not it let’s go the next thing and you know you don’t find just diamonds anywhere. You don’t find precious gems anywhere you’ve got to go searching amen amen. faqs.question: Why didn’t Israel enter God’s rest?
faqs.answer: They saw his works but did not believe.

faqs.question: What does the Red Sea crossing picture?
Who is the prophet like Moses?
Who is the bread of life?
Do we literally eat his flesh?
faqs.answer: No; it is like food that abides in us.
